question.prompt: For \(x\geq0,\) the smallest value of \(\dfrac{4x^2+8x+13}{6(1+x)}\) is:

solutions.explanation:
To test the candidate \(2\), subtract it and look for a nonnegative expression. For every \(x\geq0\), the denominator \(6(1+x)\) is positive, and
\[
\frac{4x^2+8x+13}{6(1+x)}-2
=\frac{4x^2-4x+1}{6(1+x)}
=\frac{(2x-1)^2}{6(1+x)}\geq0.
\]
Thus the expression is always at least \(2\). Equality holds when \(2x-1=0\), or \(x=1/2\), which is in the allowed domain. Therefore the smallest value is \(\boxed{2}\), choice B.
solutions.title: Compare with 2 using a square

solutions.explanation:
The numerator can be written as \(4(x+1)^2+9\), matching the denominator's \(x+1\). Set \(t=x+1\), so \(t\geq1\). The expression becomes
\[
\frac{4t^2+9}{6t}
=\frac16\left(4t+\frac9t\right).
\]
The two terms inside the parentheses are positive and have product \(36\). For positive numbers \(u,v\), expanding \((\sqrt u-\sqrt v)^2\geq0\) gives \(u+v\geq2\sqrt{uv}\), with equality exactly when \(u=v\). Applying this bound gives
\[
\frac16\left(4t+\frac9t\right)
\geq\frac16\cdot2\sqrt{36}=2.
\]
Equality requires \(4t=9/t\). Since \(t>0\), this gives \(t=3/2\), or \(x=1/2\), an allowed value. Hence the minimum is \(\boxed{2}\), choice B.
